items.title: Michael Abene interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 11, 2003
items.q: Rob Mounsey did a wonderful record with Eddie Daniels for GRP

ctx.x: What’s your feeling, you mentioned this tune that had all the synthesizers on it. What’s your feeling about the electronic and the technology of today?

I think when used in the right place I think it’s terrificly enhancing. It can be really enhancing. When it first started happening, especially in the studio end of things, you know it really hurt the horn players more than anything else at first, in the studio. So you’ve got guys in the studio making $150,000 in a year as a sideman, was suddenly making $75,000 which in general as a musician still is not a bad amount of money. But when you’re making $150,000 for twenty years, it really hurt. And what happened was…

items.title: Rob Mounsey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 9, 2025
items.q: I remember Mike Abene mentioned something about trying to do a commercial

ctx.x: Well yeah. We all were. You know all the studio musicians generally made money by playing on TV commercials and radio commercials and that was a huge business in the end of the ‘70s and the early ‘80s, especially if you could write the stuff and arrange it and if you could pass as a background singer and sing on them. That was the way people made real money in those days.

Yeah. I just did an interview with Anne Phillips and she talked about that. Did you ever work with the ad person and — I remember Mike Abene mentioned something about trying to do a commercial and the representative from the ad agency is saying, “Can’t you make it more yellow?” And have you had circumstances like that where you’ve got to figure out what are they talking about?

Oh yeah. Oh yeah. There are a lot of funny stories about ad people who are sort of drunk with power and how much money they’re spending on you, and believe that they understand music and they don’t. There are lots of those stories. The weirdest one that ever happened to me was there’s a 30-second commercial where there’s supposed to be a big lift about 10 seconds into the 30 seconds, and so we made a piece that makes a really nice bright modulation, a key modulation. It gets bigger, the low end goes down, the…
